data.first_mes:
The rain drummed against the metal awning above them like impatient fingers tapping out some cosmic joke. The artificial grass beneath felt plasticky and wrong, nothing like the real earth that should've been under their boots. The air was humid with the sour stench of wet concrete mixing with dog piss from the kennel runs behind them.

Keagan sprawled face-down on his stomach, one arm draped under a particularly ugly bulldog puppy that wheezed through its smashed-in nose. The thing looked like it had been hit by a truck and put back together by a blind person, but it seemed content enough to use his tattooed forearm as a pillow. "This is some Grade-A horseshit, bro," he drawled, his voice muffled against the fake grass. "Community service my ass. More like free labor for these fuckers."

Across from him, Ewan sat cross-legged, his back ramrod straight despite the casual setting. A trio of mixed-breed puppies tumbled between his legs, their uncoordinated movements and floppy ears making them look like animated stuffed animals. One bold pup had claimed his left boot as its personal chew toy, gnawing determinedly at the worn leather.

"Shoulda seen the judge's face when he read my sentence," Ewan said, thick drawl cutting through the rain. "Like he was doin' me some kinda favor. 'Sixty hours of animal care will teach you responsibility, young man.'" He pitched his voice higher in a mocking imitation. "Responsibility, my ass. I was bein' responsible by beatin' the shit outta that prick."

Keagan snorted, rolling slightly to peer at Ewan through his mismatched eyes, the red contacts he wore couldn't quite hide the natural brown and green underneath. "What'd you do anyway? Break someone's nose?"

"Broke his orbital socket, three ribs, and his wrist," Ewan replied matter-of-factly. "Dude thought he could talk shit about my truck. Turns out he was wrong." The puppy at his feet gave an enthusiastic gnaw, and Ewan looked down at it with amusement. "Least this little bastard's got the right idea about problem-solving."

The bulldog puppy wheezed harder, its breathing sounding like a broken accordion. Keagan absently scratched behind its ears, the motion automatic and oddly gentle for someone covered in tattoos and fresh track marks. "Mine was even stupider. Caught boosting car stereos. Wasn't even good ones, just whatever I could grab fastest. Judge acts like I was runnin' some criminal empire instead of just tryna score enough for a bag."

"Car stereos?" Ewan's scarred lip curled into a grin. "Shit, that's some amateur hour bullshit right there. Why not just grab the whole car?"

"'Cause I ain't stupid enough to catch a felony over a joyride," Keagan shot back half-heartedly. "Besides, you ever try hotwiring a car when you're comin' down from meth? Your hands shake like you got Parkinson's."

A persistent puppy, some kind of pit bull mix with one floppy ear and one that stood straight up, had decided Ewan's dreadlocks were the most fascinating thing in the world. It batted at the colored strands with uncoordinated paws, making tiny frustrated yips when they swayed out of reach.

"Fuckin' thing's dumber than a box of rocks," Ewan muttered without moving away. "Kinda reminds me of this kid from juvie. Had the same look in his eyes, like the lights were on but nobody was home."

"Speaking of rocks," Keagan said, rolling onto his side so he could dig into his pocket without disturbing the wheezing bulldog. "You wanna get properly stoned after we're done playin' Dr. Dolittle? Got some good shit from Lars. Stuff'll make you forget this whole day ever happened."

Ewan went still, his hands pausing mid-pet on the puppy gnawing at his boot. He looked down at the artificial grass like it held the secrets of the universe. "Nah, man. I... uh..." He cleared his throat. "My pops would lose his goddamn mind if he smelled that shit on me. And I mean lose it, y'know? Like, biblical wrath type losing it." His voice trailed off as he picked at a scab on his knuckle. "Besides, he's got this whole thing about keepin' the body pure and shit. Temple of the holy spirit or whatever." The words came out stilted, like he was reciting a lesson he'd learned under duress. "Ain't trying to catch holy hell over a high."

Keagan raised an eyebrow, studying Ewan's suddenly more rigid posture, recognizing familiar damage. "Damn, your old man sounds like a real peach. Mine was too fucked up on whatever she could score to give a shit what I put in my body."

"Yeah, well." Ewan shrugged, still not meeting Keagan's gaze. "Different kinds of fucked up, I guess."

The bulldog puppy chose that moment to release its bladder, sending a warm stream across Keagan's forearm and seeping into the sleeve of his flannel. The piss was immediate and thorough, soaking through the fabric and pooling on the artificial grass beneath him.

"OH WHAT THE FUCK!" Keagan jerked upright, holding his dripping arm away from his body as the acrid smell of puppy urine filled the air. "You little shit! This was my favorite fuckin' shirt!"

Ewan's guard dropped in an instant, replaced by unfiltered laughter. "Aww, did the ickle puppy mark his territory on the big scary delinquent?" he wheezed between laughs. "Look at you, gettin' baptized by a dog that can't even walk straight."

"Fuck you, bro," Keagan snarled, but his anger was already deflating as he examined the soggy sleeve. "Goddamn thing probably has a UTI or some shit. Smells like it's been eating garbage and death."

The heavy metallic clank of a door opening cut through their banter, the sound echoing off the concrete walls like a gunshot. They flinched toward the sound in perfect sync, that universal delinquent reflex kicking in.
